contract_inferred: No 00-contract.md. Inferred from the page: web, Persuade with a Read part (the product site of a design-intelligence skill, with feature cards, a tech-stack grid, a six-step walkthrough with code samples, a filterable demo gallery with 'Load More', other products and a footer). English only (html lang en at every width), no market named. No right-to-left language.
overall_reason: Cards, filter chips and code samples wrap at 375, the page stays within every budget and most text is server-rendered; about a fifth of the text still needs script, and one gallery thumbnail is served at three times its size.

score.reason: T-WIDTHS, T-HOSTILE-CONTENT and T-TRANSLATE pass, T-NO-SCRIPT loses about 20% of the text (ROB-015, citing the sweep's ROB-001 Floor) and T-WEIGHT-FOR-JOB has one oversized thumbnail (ROB-018).

findings.title: Content and navigation do not depend on script
findings.where: Whole page, scripts off, all widths
findings.evidence: With scripts off 4,211 characters are visible against 5,298 in the baseline, a share of 0.795; the scripts-off page also has 924 fewer characters in total (4,374), so part of the content is never rendered without script (resilience.hidden_content). The sweep's hidden_content hit (ROB-001, Floor) records 816 characters (16%) invisible with JavaScript off.
findings.before: Part of the page is rendered on the client after load.
findings.after: Render the remaining sections, including the first page of demos, in the static Next.js output, and keep script for filtering and 'Load More'.
findings.why: A visitor or crawler without script loses about a fifth of the page, which the product site needs for its case.

findings.title: Weight fits the page's job
findings.evidence: The Pet Grooming thumbnail is a 1,280px PNG of 333 KiB shown at 409px (3.1 times its shown width; performance.images.oversized_over_2.2x), the heaviest file on the page. The other thumbnails and the total of 853 KiB over 44 requests stay inside the budgets.
findings.before: A full-size PNG screenshot used as a gallery thumbnail.
findings.after: Serve gallery thumbnails at 1 and 2 times their shown width as WebP or AVIF through srcset (draft ROB-167), which Next.js Image does by default.
findings.why: One card costs more than the page's three largest scripts together, and each thumbnail added to the gallery in the same way repeats the cost.

strengths: At 375 the feature cards, tech-stack tiles and walkthrough steps stack cleanly, the gallery's category chips wrap onto several rows, and the code sample wraps its long class strings inside its box (tiles/375-03.png to tiles/375-07.png); the document width equals the viewport at every width.
The stylesheet favours logical properties (93 logical against 62 physical, 28 start and end rules) and has 21 min-width: 0 rules and 8 aspect-ratio rules.
Five of seven @font-face rules use font-display: swap with unicode-range subsets, and two declare metric overrides ('DM Sans Fallback').
All 14 images are lazy-loaded, and 'Load More' answered within 0.5 s with the next demos; the gallery states its count ('Showing 6 of 39 demos').
not_investigated: T-STRESS: no hostile content was injected; long demo names were judged from layout evidence.
A right-to-left render and translated strings were not captured.
The page load was not throttled and layout shift was not measured as a number (capture predates the CLS record).
The fail run of 'Load More' was skipped because the slow run made no request; the gallery filters were not exercised, so an empty filter result was not seen.
perf.json lists eight lazy thumbnails and partner logos as not loaded at measurement time, but the tiles show them drawn; not treated as failed images.
23 requests (analytics) were blocked by the capture.
Widths between the captures, landscape, zoom at 200%, back navigation and deep links.
